panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E photomicrograph of excised torus mandibularis (TM) tissue from a human patient, showing dense mature lamellar bone with lacunae and osteocytes, matching the torus mandibularis dense lamellar bone histology finding. Caption and in-text explicitly attribute the specimen to TM in an article focused on torus removal.
panels.attribution_text: Rocca et al. Er:YAG Laser: A New Technical Approach to Remove Torus Palatinus and Torus Mandibularis.. Case reports in dentistry 2012. doi:10.1155/2012/487802. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Photomicrograph of histological appearance of TM shows dense bony tissue, presence of lacunae and normal osteocytes (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification 200x).
in_text_mentions: Hard tissue fragment was submitted in 10% formalin for histopathologic examination. The examination of hematoxylin and eosin staining specimen revealed (Figure 4) dense, mature bony tissue, organized in wide lamellar pattern with scattered osteocytes and small marrow spaces.

A computed tomography (CT) scan, revealed a right torus measuring 2.40 x 1.36 cm, a left torus measuring 2.96 x 1.12 cm, and an inter-toral distance of 0.39 cm (Figure 2). The calculus's dimensions and tight spacing contributed to the obstruction of the submandibular papillae, resulting in sialadenitis. The CT scan also revealed a 0.47 cm sialolith in Wharton’s duct (Figure 3). The patient was started on a three-week course of 300 mg of clindamycin and 20 mg of prednisone, taken once daily.
